q: What is the GWP calculation methodology used in EPDs and what are its limitations for LEED V5 decision-making?
options: GWP in EPDs only includes CO₂ — other greenhouse gases are excluded
EPD GWP calculations are fully standardized and have no limitations

logic: EPD GWP calculations use a 100-year Global Warming Potential (GWP100) standardized by the IPCC. Limitations include: the 100-year horizon understates near-term warming impact of short-lived pollutants like methane, biogenic carbon treatment varies between EPD standards, and end-of-life scenarios involve uncertainty. q: What specific design principles differentiate high-quality transit-oriented development (TOD) from simply locating near a transit stop?
options: TOD only applies to projects developed by transit agencies
TOD integrates walkable streets, mixed uses, density, and pedestrian connectivity — not just proximity
TOD simply means any building within 1 mile of a transit stop
TOD is distinguished by having a bus stop directly on the project site
purpose: Assess whether the learner can apply the LT concept and solve this concept question using the governing LEED v5 intent, scope, or requirement.
vocabulary: location and transportation: strategies that reduce travel impacts through site selection and mobility options; transportation demand management: programs that reduce single-occupancy vehicle travel and parking demand
keywords: Match the term, scope, or function in the question to the exact LEED concept; decisive answer: TOD integrates walkable streets, mixed uses, density, and pedestrian connectivity — not just proximity.
logic: TOD quality is determined by the walking environment between building and transit, not just straight-line distance. A building 300m from a rail station with six traffic lanes and no crosswalks delivers little transit benefit. A building 500m away via a pleasant mixed-use pedestrian path may achieve far higher transit mode share.
